Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Jonas (serving runtime) and Grace (compliance) to make sure we cover edge cases. High level below; I'll follow up with a short sample manifest and a CSV of the field catalog attached.

What we log (admin/operator events) — representative set:
- Account & ACL changes: create/modify/delete users, role grants/revokes, group membership changes
- Authentication/authorization events: successful/failed console logins, SSO assertions, API token creation/rotation/revocation
- Privileged actions: key rotations, KMS/HSM key access events, model pin/unpin, model version rollouts, canary deploys, fallback activations
- Configuration changes: autoscale policy updates, capacity pool assignments, network policy changes (VPC peering, egress rules)
- Operator activity: manual console actions (start/stop instances, job reruns), remote debugging sessions traced to request ids
- Data-access-adjacent admin actions: data-export job starts/stops, redaction toggles, retention-policy updates

Fields captured per event (typical):
- actor.email, actor.id, actor.type (user/service)
- event.type, event.subtype
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601), event_id, request_id, correlation_id
- source.ip, source.user_agent, source.region
- target.resource_type, target.resource_id, target_namespace
- prev_state (when applicable), new_state (when applicable)
- outcome (success/failure), error_code (if any)

Retention & export options:
- Hosted: default retention 90 days for admin events. Customer tenant metadata (PII) is redacted in shared-hosted exports by default.
- Dedicated: retention configurable up to 3 years depending on reservation tier; can enable longer retention via contract addon.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): fully customer-controlled retention policy; can be set to any period and integrated directly with customer KMS/HSM.

Export formats & delivery mechanisms:
- Formats: JSONL (newline-delimited), Parquet (columnar), compressed archives (.tar.gz).
- Manifests: machine-readable manifest.jsonl with per-file checksum (sha256), record counts, time windows, sequence tokens for incremental deltas.
- Delivery: presigned S3 URLs, SFTP push, secure FTP with PGP envelope, syslog/CDC streaming to customer collector, or direct S3 mirror for Dedicated/Private.

Evidence integrity & chain-of-custody:
- Each export bundle includes a signed manifest (HMAC-SHA256 with a Redwood export key) and a detached signature file. For high-assurance handoffs we timestamp manifests with RFC3161 timestamping and provide an attestation note.
- Transport is encrypted (TLS), at-rest encryption with customer KMS when configured.
- We support proof-of-delivery: server-side logs + signed manifest + checksum verification on receipt.

Attachments I will include: admin_activity_field_catalog.csv (field-level descriptions) and later sample_admin_manifest.jsonl.

3) Grace — can you confirm wording for the SOC 2 evidence statement we'll share with auditors?

Hi Alicia — quick engineering note on export shapes and incremental strategy: we recommend incremental snapshots for active tenants to reduce bandwidth and auditing surface. Key points:

- Snapshot vs delta: full snapshot (timebox) contains a complete window (e.g., 2026-06-01T00:00Z to 2026-06-20T23:59Z). Deltas contain only events after the last sequence_token. Each exported bundle carries a start_sequence and end_sequence.
- Ordering & idempotency: every event has a strictly monotonic sequence_token and event_id; consumers can replay deltas safely and dedupe by event_id.
- Manifest fields (sample): bundle_id, start_time, end_time, record_count, file_names, file_checksums (sha256), start_sequence, end_sequence, generated_by, signature.hmac, rfc3161_timestamp (optional)
- Retention considerations: if you plan to hold for >1 year we recommend Dedicated or Private; hosted exports are possible but we retain hosted raw streams only for the configured tenant retention window.

Attached: sample_admin_manifest.jsonl (single-line JSONL snippet) and an internal script reference (we won't attach the script, but can share on request).
